Section 133 is an amending provision, but it contains two discernible target topics: a substituted Metallic Minerals Tax Act definition of mining right and repeated office-name substitutions from director to mine assessor or Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metallic Minerals Tax Act mining right definition amendment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 133(1) repeals and substitutes the definition of mining right in the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substituted Metallic Minerals Tax Act definition of mining right in this amending provision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metallic Minerals Tax Act director and mine assessor wording amendments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 133(2) to 133(10) amend multiple provisions by repealing one subsection and substituting references to mine assessor, Minister or removing director wording.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the pattern of director, mine assessor and Minister wording changes made to the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ownership of Minerals Act mining rights amendments
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections amend the Ownership of Minerals Act by changing wording about mining rights and replacing section 9 with a savings rule for specified mining rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Ownership of Minerals Act wording change and the replacement rule preserving specified mining rights.

reason: Section 136 is an amending definition provision that substitutes the Pipe Line Act definition of mineral and lists included and excluded substances.

proposedGroups.reason: The target substitutes a definition of mineral in the Pipe Line Act and lists exclusions for sand, gravel, clay, soil, ordinary stone, peat, bituminous shale, oil, gas and prescribed substances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substituted Pipe Line Act definition of mineral and its listed exclusions.

evidenceText: no mining lease shall be issued under the Mining Act, chapter M-14
Recorder has issued an order of survey

reason: The Municipalities Act definitions section covers distinct clusters: municipal officers and councils, tax-base definitions, rural community terms, and other standalone definitions such as personal information, quorum, retail business and weekly day of rest.

proposedGroups.reason: These defined terms identify municipal officers, council bodies, councillors, members, the Minister and municipality.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions for clerk, committee of council, council, councillor, member of a council, Minister and municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local service district, municipal and rural community tax base definitions
proposedGroups.reason: These definitions specify how three tax bases are computed using assessed real property values and specified exclusions or inclusions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how local service district, municipal and rural community tax bases are defined.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community council and member definitions

definedTerms: member of a rural community council

reason: Section 2 is one administration rule assigning administration of the Act to the Minister and allowing designation of persons to act on the Minister’s behalf.

proposedGroups.reason: The target states who administers the Act and the power to designate persons to act for the Minister.

reason: Section 3 separates municipal corporate continuation or creation from territorial-limit continuation and inclusion of contiguous waterfront structures.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporate continuation and creation of municipalities
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(1) and 3(3) address existing cities and towns continuing as bodies corporate and newly created municipalities becoming bodies corporate.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how existing cities and towns continue and how newly created municipalities become bodies corporate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal territorial limits and contiguous wharves, piers and similar structures
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(2) and 3(4) address continuation of territorial limits and inclusion of contiguous wharves, piers, docks, bridges, causeways, breakwaters and similar structures.
